scenes.visual: two bars, 1977 and 2016 eagle pairs, then the question
scenes.tts: In nineteen seventy-seven, a survey found only thirty-three pairs of bald eagles nesting in Virginia. In two thousand sixteen, a larger search counted one thousand and seventy pairs. A pair is two adults who use a nest. The larger search means the two counts are not a perfect match. Can people help a damaged ecosystem come back?

scenes.visual: pesticide chip, DDT breaks down to DDE, egg shell thins and cracks, few young
scenes.tts: A pesticide is a chemical used to kill pests, such as insects. D D T was a common pesticide in the United States. D D T breaks down into a related chemical called D D E. D D E can make bird eggshells thin. Very thin eagle eggshells often broke while the parents sat on them. Other eggs failed to hatch. So few young eagles were raised.

scenes.visual: red other problems, then green actions, then conservation label
scenes.tts: D D T was not the only problem. People also destroyed eagle habitat, the place where eagles live. Then people acted. In nineteen seventy-two, the United States banned most uses of D D T. Laws protected eagles and their nests. People protected the places where eagles nest. Protecting living things and their habitats so they last is called conservation.

scenes.visual: timeline 1972 to 2016, then a loop pair to young to pairs, with a break in the comparison
scenes.tts: Recovery took decades. Young eagles take several years to grow old enough to breed. New pairs raise young, and those young become pairs too. But eagles also die and face new dangers.

scenes.visual: bare bay floor, seeds scattered in a plot, plants grow and spread past the plot
scenes.tts: Restoration is helping a damaged ecosystem recover. By nineteen thirty-three, a disease and a hurricane had wiped out eelgrass in Virginia's coastal bays. Scientists spread eelgrass seeds by hand. The new plants made seeds that spread past the planted areas. A two thousand twenty study reported three thousand six hundred twelve hectares of eelgrass.
scenes.caption: Restoration is helping a damaged ecosystem recover. By 1933, a disease and a hurricane had wiped out eelgrass in Virginia's coastal bays. Scientists spread eelgrass seeds by hand. The new plants made seeds that spread past the planted areas. A 2020 study reported 3,612 hectares of eelgrass.

scenes.visual: limits as chips, then the answer: yes, with three actions and three cautions
scenes.tts: Recovery has limits. A review of four hundred studies found that damaged places often improve. Full recovery was less common while scientists watched. A recovered place can also look different from before. So can people help a damaged ecosystem come back? Yes. They can remove the cause, protect, and restore. But recovery is often slow, partial and different.
